core_claim: The same two universities that run Britain's elite split it cleanly in two — Oxford manufactures Prime Ministers, Cambridge manufactures Nobel laureates.

edt_01.label: Hook — The fork
edt_01.title: The Fork
edt_01.editorial_notes: 31/15/30/79 must be exact, never rounded. This is the spine of the whole piece — the mirror-image division.

edt_02.label: The Oxford machine
edt_02.title: The Oxford Machine
edt_02.editorial_notes: 45 of 59 = 76% Oxbridge. Keep Henry Pelham named as the single dual-attender.

edt_03.label: A college bigger than a university
edt_03.title: A College Bigger Than a University
edt_03.editorial_notes: Christ Church = 13 PMs (one college) > all of Cambridge (15). Eton+Oxford = 14. Keep college and school+university funnel distinct.

edt_04.label: When Cambridge ran politics — and stopped
edt_04.title: When Cambridge Ran Politics
edt_04.editorial_notes: Cambridge: 0 PMs since 1950, last to office Baldwin 1923. Every English-university PM since 1937 went to Oxford. This is a load-bearing turn.

edt_05.label: The ones who got out
edt_05.title: The Ones Who Got Out
edt_05.editorial_notes: Keep Lloyd George and Callaghan named and visible — they are the human counterexamples.

edt_06.label: The fairness footnote
edt_06.title: The Fairness Footnote
edt_06.editorial_notes: 39,259/31,284 must always carry the coverage-bias caveat — never present as enrolment. Per-10k normalisation sharpens the split. End on the fork holding, not a summary.
